newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries stabilise in London in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries stabilise in London in thin trade.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries stabilised in London in thin pre-Christmas trade on Friday, holding late Thursday's gains after a well-received five-year note auction.

The 30-year Treasury bond was trading at 98-29/32, yielding 6.583 percent, unchanged from Tokyo and compared with 98-28/32 in New York. March T-bond futures were down 6/32 at 113-11 in automated trade.

"We're barely changed across the curve, but the market has recovered a little on the back of a reasonable five-year auction on Thursday," said Adam Chester, international bond strategist at Yamaichi International in London.
He said London trade was very quiet with no important data scheduled apart from final third quarter real GDP data at 1330 GMT. The market forecast here is for a 2.0 percent rise.
Chester said there might be more interest in the minutes of the November 13 meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee due out at 2130 GMT.
"The minutes should highlight the fact that policy in the U.S. is on hold for the time being," he said.
That, plus the fact supply was out of the way after this week's two- and five-year auctions, might give the market a little bit of a bid to it, but in the context of quiet pre-Christmas trade.

There was some potential for volatility due to the fact that Friday was triple witching -- the quarterly expiration of options, index options and futures -- but Chester said he would be surprised to see any major move.
